fixes.explanation: I get the guess, since shepherds show up in the Christmas story (Luke 2:8-20). But this verse points somewhere else. Luke 2:21 says the name was "…the name the angel had given Him before He was conceived." So the name came first, and the angel gave it.

Shiloh, baker? Now that's a name with some history, but Luke doesn't send this family there. Luke 2:22 says His parents brought Him to Jerusalem to present Him to the Lord. I wouldn't walk into the wrong town with a baby and a pair of turtledoves, and neither would they.

Bethel is a fine name, friend, but it's not what Luke gives us. Luke 2:22 says His parents brought Him to Jerusalem to present Him to the Lord. One place is named for this trip, and it's Jerusalem. Bethel can stay on the map and out of this story.

Right, baker, and here's the proof. Luke 2:27 says, "Led by the Spirit, he went into the temple courts." The Spirit led him in, and Mary and Joseph brought in the child Jesus right then. If that's chance, then I'm just a stamper who got called out of a junk drawer by accident.
Yes, baker. Simeon says God prepared this salvation "…in the sight of all people…" That's a big, wide-open view. It isn't tucked away in a corner of the temple, and it isn't meant for just a few.

I get it, since Simeon is talking about Israel, baker. But the line doesn't say towns. It says "…the thoughts of many hearts will be revealed…" What gets revealed is the thoughts of many hearts, not anything about towns.

Asher is her tribe, baker, since Luke 2:36 calls her "…of the tribe of Asher." But the text says nothing about her staying home. Luke 2:37 says she "…never left the temple, but worshiped night and day…" So her days were spent at the temple.
Yes, baker. Luke 2:38 says Anna "…gave thanks to God…" She came forward at that moment and did it. Then she spoke about the Child to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.
That's the place, baker. Luke 2:39 says they returned "…to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth." Nazareth is home. They went back once they had done everything required by the Law of the Lord.
Hebron isn't mentioned anywhere in this passage, friend. Luke 2:39 says they returned "…to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth." That's their own town. The text points to Nazareth.
Yes, baker. Luke 2:40 says, "He was filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon Him." The Child grew and became strong, and that's how Luke ends this part of the story. A good note to end on.
